(frog-solvent)=
# frog-solvent

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-warning}`Spectroscopy & grids` Compute solvent accessible (SAS) and solvent excluded (SES) surfaces as cube files.

## What it does

Two standard molecular surfaces describe what a solvent "sees". The **solvent accessible surface
(SAS)** is traced by the centre of a solvent sphere (the *probe*, 1.4 Å ≈ water) rolling on the
atoms; the **solvent excluded surface (SES**, also called Connolly or molecular surface) is the
inner surface of the probe, i.e. the boundary of the space the solvent cannot enter. Use them for
figures (how exposed is a reactive site, a metal centre, a cavity?), to compare the size and shape of
conformers or catalysts, or to check where a larger solvent molecule fits. This command writes them
as cube files to be drawn in any viewer.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-solvent/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

Only a **geometry**: an `.xyz` file or an ORCA/Gaussian output (the last geometry is used); no
wavefunction is needed. Atomic radii are the Bondi van der Waals radii (H 1.20, C 1.70, N 1.55,
O 1.52 Å ...), optionally enlarged with `--vdw-offset`; elements missing from the table (e.g. many
transition metals) get 1.5 × their covalent radius. Choose the probe radius for your solvent with
`--probe-radius` (default 1.4 Å, water). A molecular viewer that reads cube files (VMD, ChimeraX,
Avogadro, GaussView) is needed to look at the result.

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `input` … | required | ORCA/Gaussian output or XYZ files |

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--sas-only` |  | Generate only the SAS cube |
| `--ses-only` |  | Generate only the SES cube |
| `--spacing` `SPACING` | `0.1` | Grid spacing in Å |
| `--voxels` `VOXELS` |  | Number of grid points per axis (overrides --spacing) |
| `--padding` `PADDING` | `3.0` | Box padding around the molecule in Å |
| `--probe-radius` `PROBE_RADIUS` | `1.4` | Solvent probe radius in Å |
| `--vdw-offset` `VDW_OFFSET` | `0.0` | Offset added to the Bondi vdW radius, in Å |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file) |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet`, `--format {table,json,csv}`, `--table-file PATH` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `Solvent Surface Summary` | always | One row per input file: SAS and SES cube paths |
| File | `<stem>_sas.cube` | `unless --ses-only` | Solvent accessible surface |
| File | `<stem>_ses.cube` | `unless --sas-only` | Solvent excluded surface |

### How to read it

A *Solvent Surface Summary* table with the paths of the written cubes; with the progress messages
(hidden by `-q`) each surface also reports its grid and the **enclosed volume** in Å³.

* The cube values are a **signed distance in Å** from the surface: negative inside, positive outside,
  zero on the surface; so the isovalue to draw is always 0.0 (not a density isovalue).
* The SAS is much larger than the SES: it lies one probe radius further out. SAS volume ≫ SES volume.
* Cubes are big at the default 0.1 Å spacing: about 28 MB per cube even for water; for large
  molecules use `--spacing 0.2` or `--voxels 100` for a preview. A coarse grid makes the SES slightly
  bumpy and its volume less accurate.

Example (`water.xyz`, defaults): 135×126×120 grid; SAS volume 124.50 Å³, SES volume 19.85 Å³,
two cubes of 28.6 MB each.

## Step by step

1. Run `frog-solvent mol.xyz`: writes `mol_sas.cube` and `mol_ses.cube` next to the input (`--out-dir surfaces` to collect them elsewhere; `--sas-only` or `--ses-only` for one of the two).
2. Adjust the probe (`--probe-radius 1.9` for a bulkier solvent) and the grid: `--spacing` (Å, default 0.1) or `--voxels N` per axis, `--padding` (Å, default 3.0).
3. In the viewer, load the cube together with the molecule and draw the isosurface at value **0.0**.

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-solvent --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-solvent --help`
```text
usage: frog-solvent [-h] [-v] [-q] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--table-file PATH]
                    [--sas-only | --ses-only] [--spacing SPACING] [--voxels VOXELS]
                    [--padding PADDING] [--probe-radius PROBE_RADIUS] [--vdw-offset VDW_OFFSET]
                    [--out-dir DIR]
                    input [input ...]

Compute solvent accessible (SAS) and solvent excluded (SES) surfaces as cube files.

The cubes hold a signed distance field (Å, negative inside the surface): plot the 0.0 isosurface.
Atomic radii are Bondi vdW radii plus --vdw-offset (default 0).

positional arguments:
  input                        ORCA/Gaussian output or XYZ files

options:
  -h, --help                   show this help message and exit
  --sas-only                   Generate only the SAS cube
  --ses-only                   Generate only the SES cube
  --spacing SPACING            Grid spacing in Å (default: 0.1)
  --voxels VOXELS              Number of grid points per axis (overrides --spacing)
  --padding PADDING            Box padding around the molecule in Å (default: 3.0)
  --probe-radius PROBE_RADIUS  Solvent probe radius in Å (default: 1.4)
  --vdw-offset VDW_OFFSET      Offset added to the Bondi vdW radius, in Å (default: 0.0)

output:
  -v, --verbose                Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet                  Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  --format {table,json,csv}    Format of the tables printed on stdout (default: table)
  --table-file PATH            Also write all tables to PATH (.json, .csv or .txt; otherwise the
                               --format is used)
  --out-dir DIR                Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input
                               file)

outputs:
  terminal (stdout; --format table|json|csv, --table-file PATH):
    Solvent Surface Summary     One row per input file: SAS and SES cube paths
  files (next to each input, or --out-dir):
    <stem>_sas.cube             [unless --ses-only] Solvent accessible surface
    <stem>_ses.cube             [unless --sas-only] Solvent excluded surface

examples:
  frog-solvent opt.out
      SAS and SES cubes next to opt.out
  frog-solvent mol.xyz --sas-only --probe-radius 1.9 --voxels 100
      SAS for a larger probe on a 100x100x100 grid
  frog-solvent conf_*.xyz --out-dir surfaces
      Surfaces of several conformers in surfaces/

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-solvent.md.
```
:::
